Make the edit. Own the release.

Turn your footage into a finished story, give each platform its own version, and keep the next release moving from one workspace.

An edit you can keep editing

Trim footage, arrange video and graphics, adjust sound, and work with layers and keyframes in Studio. Save the project, return to its timeline, and export the result.

Build titles and logo artwork, animate individual pieces and shape their timing. Motion, Graphics and the timeline work on the same editable project.

Sound that belongs to the picture

Place music and effects on the programme clock. Adjust cue timing, levels and fades, then check the complete export with sound.

pages.text:
ANALYTICS / LEARN FROM THE RELEASE

See what happened after Publish.

Put publication state and available platform performance together, so your next creative decision has something real behind it.

01
Start with the actual post

Inspect the release and its destinations. A scheduled post, an upload being processed and a published video represent different stages of the journey.

Understand post states
↗
02
Keep the numbers meaningful

Views, impressions, reactions and other metrics mean different things across platforms. A measured zero stays zero; a number the provider has not returned is unavailable.

Get analytics help
↗
03
Compare, then make the next edit

Look at the available results for each destination and allow for reporting delays. Use those observations to revise the opening, pacing or packaging of your next video.

Return to the edit
↗
Know what the dashboard can tell you.

Metric availability and refresh timing depend on the platform, permissions and your plan. The dashboard does not guarantee reach, revenue attribution or audience growth. Check the source and reporting period before comparing posts.

Room for your next creation.

Pricing
Back

Plans are based on publishing volume, connected platform limits, editing access, and monthly credits. Drafting and planning can stay lightweight, while heavier server renders use credits so you always know what costs compute before you run it.

Starter Is Limited

Starter includes 15 monthly credits, 3 uploads, and 1 connected platform. Multi-camera editing and the premium creative suite start on paid plans.

Paid Plans Include Credits

Paid plans include the monthly credits and limits shown on each plan card below. Higher tiers add more credits, platform connections, uploads, seats, analytics, and support.

Renders Spend Credits

Drafting scenes and shot lists can stay lightweight, but server renders, AI video previews, clip analysis, clean-audio sync, and MP4 exports spend credits.

PRODUCT NOTES / DEVELOPMENT UPDATES

The details keep moving forward.

Recent work on editing, publishing and the documentation around them. Check the running app and guides for availability in your account.

21 October 2026

Clearer controls. More useful guides.

Studio inspector layouts keep Graphics and Sound controls inside the panel. Motion fields and sound cues are easier to read. The refreshed guides cover inspector navigation, keyframes, Logo Workshop and sound-cue editing.

21 October 2026

A clearer picture of a release.

Publishing and analytics work distinguishes scheduled, processing and published states, preserves unavailable metrics separately from real zeroes, and keeps destination copy and timing visible.

18 October 2026

More ways to build motion.

Studio development adds editable vector artwork, stroke trim and offset, text choreography and Logo Workshop. These use ordinary layers and keys in the same project; capability-specific limits remain in the guides.

These are development updates, not a guarantee that every change is deployed to every account. Read the capability guides for scope and limitations.

ABOUT / MORE TIME FOR THE WORK

Publishing should leave room for creating.

A strong edit is only part of the job. Creators also have to prepare each post, move between accounts, remember release times and make sense of the response.

01
Make the work yours

Studio brings footage, sound, typography and motion into an editable timeline. Keep control of the decisions that make the story feel like you.

Meet the tools
↗
02
Give it a thoughtful release

Publisher and the schedule connect the finished media to individual destinations, with each platform’s copy and timing visible.

See the publishing flow
↗
03
Learn from what happened

Publication records and available analytics help you follow the release. They are evidence to work with, rather than a promise that an algorithm will reward every post.

Understand the feedback
↗
Built around the complete creator workflow.

AutoPromote brings making, publishing and reviewing into one place. The aim is practical: spend less of your day repeating the same publishing steps, and more of it making work people want to watch.

TRUST / PRIVACY

Privacy Policy

How account, content and connected-platform information is handled.

Effective date: December 10, 2025 (Last Updated: November 15, 2025)

Note: This is a draft policy for transparency and platform review. It does not constitute legal advice. For compliance matters, contact us at thulani@autopromote.org.

1. Introduction

Welcome to AutoPromote ("we", "us", or "our"). We are committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you use our application and services. Please read this policy carefully. If you do not agree, do not use the Service.

2. Data Controller & Contact

The data controller for AutoPromote is AutoPromote. For privacy inquiries or to exercise your rights, contact: thulani@autopromote.org.

3. What We Collect

We collect the following categories of information:

Account information: name, email address, profile details you provide.
User Content: content you create, schedule, or upload through the Service (e.g., posts, captions, media).
Authentication & Usage: login tokens, IP address, device and browser metadata, and usage logs.
Payment Data: billing identifiers and transaction records required to process payments (we do not store full card numbers; payments are processed by PayPal).
Social Network Data: information you choose to share from connected social accounts (profile, public posting permissions) when you link third-party platforms.
4. How We Use Your Information

We use personal data to operate and improve the Service, including to:

Create and manage your account and provide core features.
Post or schedule content on third-party platforms where you grant permission.
Process payments and refunds through third-party payment processors.
Communicate about your account, updates, or security issues.
Analyze and improve functionality, detect fraud, and enforce policies.
5. Third-Party Processors

We use third-party service providers to operate the Service. Key processors include:

Firebase / Google: authentication, database, storage.
Resend or SendGrid: transactional email delivery.
PayPal: payment processing.
Analytics providers: usage analytics and performance monitoring.

We share the minimum data necessary with these processors and require them to protect personal data under contract.

6. Your Rights

Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or export your personal data, and to object to certain processing. To exercise your rights, contact us at thulani@autopromote.org. We will respond within a reasonable timeframe as required by applicable law.

7. Retention

We retain personal data as long as necessary to provide the Service and for legitimate business or legal purposes (for example, to comply with legal obligations or resolve disputes). For account deletion requests we generally remove account data within 30–90 days, but some backups or aggregated analytics may be retained longer in anonymized form.

8. Cookies & Tracking

We use cookies and similar technologies for authentication, security, and analytics. You can control cookies through your browser settings; disabling cookies may limit features.

9. Security

We use commercially reasonable technical and administrative measures (such as TLS in transit and least-privilege for service accounts) to protect personal data. No system is perfect — if you suspect a security issue, contact thulani@autopromote.org.

10. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy. We will post the new effective date at the top of this page. Material changes will be highlighted or emailed to users where required.

11. Contact Us

If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at: thulani@autopromote.org.

What your browser remembers.

AutoPromote uses browser storage as well as cookies and similar technologies. They serve different purposes, from keeping you signed in to retaining an editable project on your device.

01
Sign-in and preferences

Authentication storage helps retain your session. The app also remembers selected preferences on your device. Browser storage restrictions can affect sign-in and saved settings.

02
Locally saved Studio projects

Studio stores saved projects in your browser. Clearing site data or changing browser profiles can remove those local copies. Download a project backup before clearing storage.

Save and back up a project

Third-party services

Connected sign-in providers, payment pages and external platforms apply their own storage and privacy practices. Review the notices presented when using those services.

Manage storage in your browser.

Use your browser’s privacy and site-data settings to inspect or remove stored data. Signing out, clearing local projects and revoking a connected account are different actions. For a privacy request, contact thulani@autopromote.org.
